events.why_here: The opening raid and Trinity's breakout through the hotel, across the rooftops, and out through the phone booth form one continuous chase; it resolves when she escapes and the Agents pivot to their new lead, 'Neo.'

events.working_title: Neo Is Summoned and Meets Trinity
events.why_here: The story shifts from the Agents to Neo: the machine messages summon him via the white rabbit, and the party confrontation with Trinity ends the beat by posing the unanswered question 'What is the Matrix?'

A new situation begins with Neo waking late for work; the office pursuit, failed ledge escape, arrest, and interrogation with the mouth-sealing and bug implant are one captured-and-coerced arc, ending when the bug takes hold and the scene cuts away.

Neo waking from the apparent nightmare resets the situation; he commits to meeting Morpheus, is collected by Trinity's crew, and submits to their custody in the car, launching a new journey whose destination is still ahead.

The journey pauses for a discrete medical operation — removing the tracker from Neo's body — and ends once the bug is expelled and the tap is shed, a self-contained unit before the party reaches its destination.

The car reaches the Hotel Lafayette and Neo is led to Morpheus; the whole run builds to and resolves on the single irreversible decision — swallowing the red pill — after which a different question (what happens next) begins.

The trace program activates and Neo is physically dragged out of the Matrix — through the mirror, the pod, the waste line, and into the hovercraft — one continuous extraction that ends when he reaches the ship and collapses.

Neo regains consciousness and is gradually oriented to his new body, the year, and the ship; this recuperative run answers 'am I alive / where am I' and ends as Morpheus leads him to the main deck for the full revelation.

Neo is jacked into the Construct and shown what the Matrix and the real world truly are; the explanatory run culminates in his rejection and physical collapse back on the deck, closing the revelation and its immediate aftermath.

A pivot: Neo accepts there is no return and Morpheus reframes the rescue as the fulfillment of prophecy, ending when he names Neo's 'training' — the question shifts from 'why was I freed' to 'what now,' which the next scenes answer.

The training day begins with the lights coming on and Neo meeting Tank, one unit of orientation that ends once Neo knows his operator, Zion, and the born-free crew — the question of 'who runs me and what is this resistance' is answered, and the next scene begins the actual loading of skills.

Cutting between the loading chair and Morpheus's arrival is one continuous action of downloading skills; the unit ends when Neo declares 'I know kung fu' and Morpheus says 'Show me' — the question of 'can skills be installed' is answered, and what follows tests them.

The dojo fight and its observers form one escalating confrontation — Neo learns the rules can be bent, is beaten, rages, and finally lands a blow — ending when Morpheus reframes the lesson as 'freeing the mind' and orders the jump program, a clear turn to a new test.

Cutting between the rooftop and the watching crew during one continuous leap is one event; it ends when Neo falls short, bounces on the yielding ground, and grasps that he failed because he didn't believe he would — the question of 'can he free his mind to jump' is answered, and the aftermath deals with the consequences.

events.working_title: The Cost of Dying in the Matrix
events.why_here: A pivot: the crew disperses and Neo, unplugged and bleeding, learns that 'the body cannot live without the mind' — the question of 'what happens if you die in there' is answered, closing the training sequence, and what follows is the quiet aftermath and the crew's reaction to Neo.

The aftermath of the training day: Trinity's tender caretaking spills into the hall where Cypher voices his suspicion and raises the Oracle, one unit of crew reaction to Neo that ends the sequence on a new question — whether Neo is truly the One and Cypher's growing resentment.

This is a self-contained lesson — Neo is shown Agents are beatable because they obey rules — that ends on its own cliff (Tank's 'We got trouble'). The next scene cuts away from the program entirely to the ship in motion, answering a different question: a real threat is coming.

A single continuous action — the ship speeding, the Squiddy sweeping in, the dive into the supply line, the silent EMP wait, the machine passing overhead, then the crew finally able to sleep — resolves as one survival beat. The question changes once they are safe and asleep: now it turns to Cypher's disillusionment, voiced to Neo on the main deck.

Cypher's private confession to Neo (Morpheus's five dead 'Ones') and his simultaneous betrayal bargain with Smith in the restaurant are intercut as one unit of treachery. That thread closes once the deal is sealed; the story then resets to ordinary ship life at breakfast before Morpheus announces the Oracle mission.

From Morpheus announcing the Oracle trip, through the crew jacking in and materializing in the Matrix, the car ride, and Cypher's secret phone-drop, this is one journey-and-arrival unit. It resolves when they reach the destination building; the next scene is a mood-setting exterior that opens the approach to the Oracle's floor.

The establishing shot of the building, the blind man's nod, the elevator ascent, the hallway test of faith, and the waiting room with the Spoon Boy form one continuous approach into the Oracle's domain, each step moving Neo closer to the audience. No further scene follows, so the run ends with the Priestess summoning him.

The private session delivers the two life-changing revelations (Neo is 'not the One'; Morpheus will die for him), a pivot that ends the audience; the next scene is its immediate aftermath with Morpheus.

events.working_title: Departure and Return to the Hotel
events.why_here: The group leaves the Oracle, seals the secret, and drives back to the exit; the arrival on the city street and Cypher's betraying sweat closes the return before the trap is sprung.

events.working_title: The Déjà Vu Reveals the Trap
events.why_here: The crossing cuts between the crew and Tank as one continuous realization—the glitch, the helicopters, and Tank's 'It's a trap!'—which answers 'what's happening?' and shifts the story into open danger.
The trap executes: arming up, the hardline cut, Mouse cornered and killed. This violent action beat resolves with his death, after which the survivors regroup to find their own escape blocked.

events.working_title: Cornered, Morpheus Calls for a Way Out
events.why_here: With the stairwell and windows sealed, Morpheus accepts the trap and pivots to finding an exit via a blueprint—a new problem (how do we get out?) replacing the prior fight for survival.

events.working_title: The Agents Pinpoint the Eighth Floor
events.why_here: Smith's call-trace locates the fugitives on the eighth floor, and the police/agents converge there — the hunters now know exactly where to strike.

events.working_title: Cops Find the Hole; the Crew Descends the Wall
events.why_here: The search discovers the escape hole, and the crew has already slipped into the plumbing wall — the manhunt now tracks them into the structure.

events.working_title: The Jacket, and the Question 'Where Are They?'
events.why_here: The agents find only the abandoned jacket, pausing the pursuit on the open question of the fugitives' hiding place before the sound gives them away.
A cop hears whispers through the plaster, the wall bulges, and the hiding place is exposed — turning a quiet search into an active breach.
Discovery erupts into open gunfire — Neo blasts back and the cop is seized mid-fight — the confrontation now fully violent.

The escape from the Agent — Morpheus pinning Smith so Neo can flee, and the crew descending into the basement — resolves when Morpheus is overwhelmed and taken; the story's question shifts from 'will they get out' to 'what happened to those left behind.'
The action cuts from the field to the ship for a single beat of grief — Tank reaching for the screen and crying 'No!' — a reaction pivot before the next thread (Cypher's survival) begins.

events.working_title: The Survivors Regroup and Locate an Exit
events.why_here: Trinity surfaces, Cypher reaches Tank demanding an exit, Trinity checks in, and the scattered survivors converge on the plan to reach Franklin and Erie; this unit of 'where is everyone and how do we get out' closes once they're moving toward the exit and know Cypher's location.

events.working_title: Cypher Exits First and the Crew Follows
events.why_here: The story moves from planning the escape to executing it — Cypher reaches and enters the TV repair shop, Tank jacks him out, and the others begin crawling through the ringing phone — a single continuous exfiltration that ends the moment Cypher is awake on the deck and reaching for the rifle.

events.working_title: Cypher's Betrayal and the Crew's Murder
events.why_here: Cutting between the shop (dead phone) and the deck (Cypher shooting Tank and Dozer, then killing the jacked-in crew), this is one sustained confrontation — the revelation of the betrayal and its bloody climax — that resolves when the revived Tank blasts Cypher off his feet.

events.working_title: The Crew Regroups and Decides to Rescue Morpheus
events.why_here: From Neo and Trinity's brief reunion through the crew's grief, the Agents' escalating interrogation, and finally Neo's decision to go back in, these scenes form one continuous response to Morpheus's capture. The situation stays fixed on the same problem — Morpheus is taken, the crew must react — until Neo commits to the rescue and the plan begins to load.

events.working_title: The Assault on the Government Building
events.why_here: The ominous exterior beat launches the execution of the rescue plan. From the lobby firefight through the elevator shaft ascent, the roof battle with Agent Jones, and the helicopter pilot program, every scene is one continuous action — breaking into the building to reach Morpheus — cutting between the attackers and the reacting Agents as a single unit.

events.working_title: Helicopter Assault, Morpheus's Rescue, and the Crash
events.why_here: The rescue-and-escape sequence (blasting the office, saving the falling Morpheus, the helicopter's destruction) completes with the heroes swinging free; the next scene is a reaction beat aboard the hovercraft, shifting from the escape action to its aftermath and the crew's realization.

events.working_title: The Crew Regroups; an Exit Is Secured
events.why_here: Tank's proclamation, the rooftop belief-beat, and the call arranging the subway exit form one regrouping unit; the next scene returns to the Agents in pursuit, restarting the threat rather than continuing the heroes' recovery.

events.working_title: The Agents Arrive Too Late and Order the Strike
events.why_here: The Agents find the rooftop empty, order a Sentinel strike, and Smith lingers in frustration; the next scene moves to the subway where the heroes begin exiting, answering a different question (the escape) than this unit (the pursuers' failed catch).

events.working_title: The Subway Ambush — Trinity Escapes, Neo Is Trapped
events.why_here: The ambush that separates the group (Trinity and Morpheus exit, Neo is cornered by Smith) resolves with Neo turned at gunpoint; the next scene is a reaction beat aboard the hovercraft, shifting to the crew's response rather than the station standoff.

events.working_title: The Crew Urges Neo to Believe
events.why_here: Trinity's "Run, Neo" and Morpheus's "He's beginning to believe" form one observation-beat unit focused on Neo's awakening; the next scene returns to the station for the physical fight, restarting action rather than continuing the watching.

events.working_title: Neo and Smith's Gun-and-Fist Duel to the Train
events.why_here: This is the final scene; the duel, the choke-hold by the third-rail, and the train's arrival that lets Neo break free and flee form one continuous fight-and-escape unit.

The crew realizes Neo is lost and then the sentinels are spotted, forcing the EMP decision. This unit ends once the stakes are set (charge the EMP, but not until Neo is out). The next scene returns to Neo's flight, a different thread.

A single continuous chase: Neo grabs a phone, is pursued through streets, market, and building while Tank guides him to the exit door. The unit ends when he reaches the fire escape and Tank confirms he's almost there. The next scene cuts to Smith recognizing the hotel, shifting the thread to the pursuer.
A pivot beat where Smith halts, sensing where Neo is headed. It stands apart from the chase and from the ship's EMP climax, bridging the two by foreshadowing Smith's arrival at the exit.

events.working_title: The sentinels attack; the EMP is readied
events.why_here: The red alarm sounds and the sentinels physically strike the ship, culminating in Morpheus arming the EMP and affirming Neo will make it. This is the payoff of the EMP decision set up in sc-185–186 and closes the ship thread.

The chase up the fire escape, through the window into the hall, and the crew's report that the hull is breached are one running pursuit; it ends when Neo reaches door 303 and is cornered by Smith, which begins a new, static confrontation.

Shooting, falling, the death confirmation, and Smith's 'Good-bye, Mr. Anderson' are one unit — Neo's death and its verification — resolved before Trinity's declaration over his body begins a new beat.

Trinity's confession and kiss, Neo's eyes snapping open, and the crew's 'miracle' reaction are one continuous resurrection beat; it ends once the story pivots back to Neo standing in the hall, now seeing the Matrix's code.

events.working_title: Neo Sees the Code and Destroys Smith
events.why_here: Halting the bullets, seeing the code, and killing Smith while the other Agents flee are one unit of Neo's awakening to his power; it ends when the focus returns to the doomed main deck, a different situation.

Trinity's cry, Morpheus turning the key as the sentinel descends, and the sentinels falling dead in the overflow pit are one continuous action — the firing and effect of the EMP — resolved before the ship goes still.

This single scene is a pivot: the ship is quiet, Neo revives and reunites with Trinity, and his phone broadcast reframes the whole conflict — a self-contained resolution beat distinct from the escape that follows.
The final image — Neo hanging up, stepping out, and flying above the city — is a standalone closing beat that answers a new question (what the One now does) rather than continuing the revival scene.
